 Record warmth, then rainy and turning colder this weekend 
 Your First Alert Weather Forecast: 
 The record high for November 20 is 62 degrees. By Steve Beylon Published : Nov. 20, 2026 at 6:29 AM CST | Updated : 5 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google Record warmth is possible today. Wisconsin’s statewide gun-deer hunting season opens tomorrow, with warm and windy weather in the forecast. Hunters should be mindful of high fire danger. Rain is in the forecast later this weekend, followed by a much colder start to next week.
 Record Warmth Today 
 Sunshine will mix with high clouds today. Highs will climb into the low to mid-60s. Most high temperatures will be nearly 25 degrees warmer than normal for late November. Green Bay’s record high for today is 62°, set in 2003. That record could be broken.
 Tonight will stay fair and mild, with a south breeze at times. Lows will settle in the low 50s.
 Deer Season Starts Warm And Windy 
 Clouds will thicken tomorrow as the gun-deer season gets underway. It will be windy and warm again, with highs in the mid-60s. Gusty south winds and dry soils will create a high fire danger. Take extra care with campfires and anything that could accidentally throw a spark.
 Rain will arrive late in the day, especially northwest of the Fox Valley. Those at deer camp should also be prepared for developing wet weather. Rain is likely Sunday morning before some clearing. It will turn breezy, with temperatures falling during the afternoon. Highs will be in the lower 50s.
 Colder Air And Holiday Travel 
 Monday will be partly sunny and much colder. A few flakes are possible across the Northwoods. There will be less wind, with highs in the upper 30s. It’s time to find the winter coats again before heading back to work or school.
 Tuesday will be cold but calm, with a mix of sun and clouds. Highs will be in the mid-30s. Clouds will hold on Wednesday. A spotty light rain-snow mix is possible on the day before Thanksgiving. Any precipitation looks light and spotty right now, with hopefully minimal impact on holiday travel. There’s still uncertainty in the forecast, so holiday travelers and their families should follow our First Alert updates.
 Thanksgiving will be mostly sunny and seasonably cool, with highs in the low 40s.
 Bottom line: Record warmth is possible today. Hunters should be mindful of the wind and high fire danger as deer season begins. Rain arrives late Saturday, with colder air following early next week.
 Check it out, your favorite weather graphics are in our First Alert Map Room. You can find that here: First Alert Map Room .
 You can always keep our forecast handy with our free weather app. Look for the WBAY First Alert Weather App in the Apple app store and Google Play.
 WIND FORECAST
 TODAY: S 5-10 MPH, GUSTS TO 20 MPH
 SATURDAY: S/SW 10-20 MPH, GUSTS TO 30 MPH
 LOCAL WEATHER THIS WEEK
 TODAY: Sunshine mixed with high clouds. Record warmth possible. HIGH: 65
 TONIGHT: Fair and mild. Breezy at times. LOW: 53
 SATURDAY: Clouds thicken. Windy and warm again. Late rain, especially NORTHWEST of the Fox Valley. HIGH: 65 LOW: 47
 SUNDAY: Morning rain likely, then some clearing. Turning breezy, with falling afternoon temperatures. HIGH: 51 LOW: 30
 MONDAY: A few flakes NORTH. Partly sunny. Colder, but less wind. HIGH: 38 LOW: 20
 TUESDAY: A mix of sun and clouds. Cold, but calm. HIGH: 35 LOW: 22
 WEDNESDAY: Cloudy skies. A spotty light mix? HIGH: 39 LOW: 28
 THANKSGIVING: Mostly sunny. Seasonably cool. HIGH: 41
